speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your symptoms of inappropriate behavior, changes in eating habits, and weight gain, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if you have experienced any changes in your sleep patterns or energy levels?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male. The patient has demonstrated inappropriate behavior, including making unfitting comments and attempts to kiss strangers, over the past 6 months. He shows disinterest in family interactions and has developed a particular craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, resulting in a 10 kg weight gain. The patient also presents as unkempt.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. I would like to inquire if the patient has experienced any recent memory lapses, difficulty with complex tasks, or changes in his sense of smell or taste?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inappropriate behavior. I also have Disinterest in family interactions, Craving for specific foods, Significant weight gain, Apathy, Blunted affect.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has there been any decline in your ability to perform daily tasks or manage finances, and do you have a history of alcohol use or head injuries? I will also order a brain MRI to look for structural changes. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal MRI rules out structural lesions, so I am now focusing on cognitive decline patterns. Have you noticed any difficulties with short-term memory, language, or spatial orientation, or has your personality change been the primary issue?

REQUEST TEST: Neuropsychological_Evaluation

speaker: Doctor
text:
It is unusual for the neuropsychological evaluation to be entirely normal given the behavioral changes, so I need to rule out metabolic causes. Have you been tested for thyroid function or vitamin deficiencies, and do you experience any morning stiffness or joint pain?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Function_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal thyroid results help rule out hypothyroidism as the cause of his apathy and weight gain. Given the prominent behavioral disinhibition, hyperorality, and personality changes in a 55-year-old, I suspect Frontotemporal Dementia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontotemporal Dementia
